howTo: Enter the simply-supported beam length (mm) and the midpoint concentrated load (kN).
Select the cross-section geometry: rectangular (width b × height h) or solid circular (diameter d).
Enter the material Young's modulus E (MPa) and yield strength Re (MPa). Typical structural steel defaults are 210 000 MPa and 355 MPa.
The tool calculates maximum bending moment, section modulus, second moment of area, bending stress, mid-span deflection, and static safety factor.
formula: M_max = F·L / 4 | σ = M_max / W | W_rect = b·h² / 6 | W_circle = π·d³ / 32 | I_rect = b·h³ / 12 | I_circle = π·d⁴ / 64 | δ_max = F·L³ / (48·E·I) | n = Re / σ

examples.title: Simply-supported steel rectangular beam under midpoint load
examples.description: A 500 mm steel beam with a 40 × 8 mm rectangular cross-section carries a 2 kN load at mid-span. Material: S355 (Re = 355 MPa, E = 210 000 MPa).
notes: σ > Re produces a safety factor < 1.0, highlighting that this cross-section is undersized for the applied load.
Increasing beam depth h produces a cubic increase in moment of inertia I and quadratic increase in section modulus W.

examples.title: Solid circular steel shaft as a simply-supported beam
examples.description: A 300 mm shaft with a 30 mm diameter carries a 0.5 kN central load. Material: C45 (Re = 600 MPa, E = 210 000 MPa).
notes: A high static safety factor indicates adequate static bending capacity; shaft deflection and torsional fatigue should be verified separately.
For circular sections only the diameter input is used in the calculation.

commonMistakes: Using total beam depth (h) instead of the distance to the extreme fiber (c = h/2) when deriving section modulus.
Mixing units: entering beam span in metres and cross-section in millimetres without converting force or length consistently.
Evaluating static bending stress alone while omitting deflection limits, lateral-torsional buckling, or cyclic fatigue.
assumptions: Beam is simply supported at both ends with a single concentrated load at mid-span.
Linear elastic material response according to Hooke's Law; no plastic deformation.
Slender beam geometry satisfying Euler–Bernoulli beam theory (span-to-depth ratio L/h ≥ 10).
Self-weight of the beam is negligible compared to the applied load.
